messages.subject: Error with dependent variable transformation
parts:
stack_est <- inla.stack(data = list(y = Snow$`Snow Water Equivalent (in) Start of Month Values`),
                        A = list(A,1),
                        effects = list(c(si, list(Intercept = 1)),
                                       list(data.frame(Change_depth = Snow$`Change In Snow Depth (in)`,
                                                       Air_avg = Snow$`Air Temperature Average (degF)`,
                                                       Max_air = Snow$`Air Temperature Maximum (degF)`,
                                                       Min_air = Snow$`Air Temperature Minimum (degF)`,
                                                       M = Snow$MM,
                                                       elev = Snow$elev,
                                                       SnowYear = Snow$SnowYear,
                                                       SnowD = Snow$`Snow Depth (in) Start of Month Values`))),
                        tag = "est")


formula <- log(y) ~ -1 + Intercept +
  Air_avg + elev + SnowYear + Change_depth +
  f(Spatial.field, 
    model = spde,
    control.group = list(model = "ar1"))


r <- inla(formula, 
          data = inla.stack.data(stack_est, spde = spde),
          family = "gaussian", 
          control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack_est), compute = T),
          verbose = T)

(s <- summary(r))

So that is my code, the issue i am having is when I run the data through the model it dose just fine till i notice that i have issues with constant variance, in this case I need to keep this as a linear model so i need the assumption of a constant variance. So before i log transform i am getting this.


Pre- transform y

Post transform y

 
Ok, so i transform the data and when i try the model using base r lm things work our just fine, but for this i need a spatial aspect and INLA provides a nice setting for spatial work but when i run the model again with the log transform i get this error. How can i transform my data to fix my variance and use a spatial model.

On Thursday, March 14, 2019 at 7:04:48 PM UTC-6, Clinton Woods wrote:




stack_est <- inla.stack(data = list(y = Snow$`Snow Water Equivalent (in) Start of Month Values`),
                        A = list(A,1),
                        effects = list(c(si, list(Intercept = 1)),
                                       list(data.frame(Change_depth = Snow$`Change In Snow Depth (in)`,
                                                       Air_avg = Snow$`Air Temperature Average (degF)`,
                                                       Max_air = Snow$`Air Temperature Maximum (degF)`,
                                                       Min_air = Snow$`Air Temperature Minimum (degF)`,
                                                       M = Snow$MM,
                                                       elev = Snow$elev,
                                                       SnowYear = Snow$SnowYear,
                                                       SnowD = Snow$`Snow Depth (in) Start of Month Values`))),
                        tag = "est")


formula <- log(y) ~ -1 + Intercept +
  Air_avg + elev + SnowYear + Change_depth +
  f(Spatial.field, 
    model = spde,
    control.group = list(model = "ar1"))


r <- inla(formula, 
          data = inla.stack.data(stack_est, spde = spde),
          family = "gaussian", 
          control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack_est), compute = T),
          verbose = T)

(s <- summary(r))

So that is my code, the issue i am having is when I run the data through the model it dose just fine till i notice that i have issues with constant variance, in this case I need to keep this as a linear model so i need the assumption of a constant variance. So before i log transform i am getting this.


Pre- transform y

Post transform y

 
Ok, so i transform the data and when i try the model using base r lm things work our just fine, but for this i need a spatial aspect and INLA provides a nice setting for spatial work but when i run the model again with the log transform i get this error. How can i transform my data to fix my variance and use a spatial model.
